A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same unified-label discourse probing study. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original DISRPT experiments with 23 LLMs and DisCoDisCo, including multilingual transfer, layer-wise probing, and error analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds attention-representation and pooling ablations in Appendix D, Tables 4–5.

M1.justification: The 17-label mapping, maximum-pooled within-span and between-span attention representations, MLP probe, loss, and windowing procedure remain unchanged. Alternative representations and pooling strategies are evaluated as ablations; the adopted method remains the same.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DISRPT collection covering 13 languages and four frameworks. Table 1 contains the same 26 dataset entries; v2's explicit reference to 26 datasets does not represent added coverage.

E2.justification: The 23 LLMs and jointly trained and dataset-specific DisCoDisCo systems are retained. Tables 4–5 add within-method comparators: inter-span-only and intra-span-only representations, mean pooling, and concatenated mean/maximum pooling.

E3.justification: The new ablations introduce controlled changes to attention subsets and pooling strategies while training on the existing full DISRPT collection. The established main evaluation, model configurations, training budgets, and window settings are retained.

E4.justification: v1 includes layer-wise, error, and probe-weight analyses but no representation or pooling ablations. v2 adds two systematic ablations across all 23 LLMs, testing the contributions of within-span versus between-span attention and the performance versus representation-size tradeoff of pooling choices.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-run means and retain the same error-bar plots. Tables 4–5 also report five-run averages, without introducing different run counts, seed reporting, uncertainty estimation, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Tables 4–5 add systematic cross-model results absent from v1. For Aya-23-35B, Table 4 reports 53.7% for inter-span-only, 45.5% for intra-span-only, and 58.2% for combined attention; Table 5 reports 54.2%, 58.2%, and 58.4% for mean, maximum, and combined pooling. Existing Table 3 scores and plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: No mathematical assumptions, proofs, or substantive derivations are added or revised. The new explicit flatten-and-concatenate equation restates the representation already specified in v1.

C1.justification: The central unified-label, multilingual generalization, and intermediate-layer claims are retained. Section 7 modestly broadens the stated contribution by presenting the method as useful for other linguistic questions expressible through consecutive spans.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly qualifies that discourse processing need not occur exclusively in attention layers and proposes language-specific output-layer features as an explanation for the final-layer recovery. It adds potential applications and removes Appendix D's Ju et al.-based interpretation of lower versus upper layers. The main limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4 and the new schematic explicitly explain that model outputs are ignored, no decoding strategy is imposed, and attention involving context tokens is excluded from the pooled features. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, runtimes, repository access, and licenses are retained.

R1.justification: v2 expands its distinction from Bunt and Prasad's coverage and clarifies ATTRIBUTION's relationship to that taxonomy. It adds Carlson et al. (2003), Miao et al. (2024), Deletang et al. (2024), and Skean et al. (2025), and removes Ju et al. (2024). The overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Targeted expansions affect related work, method explanation, layer-wise interpretation, the conclusion, and ATTRIBUTION documentation. There are wording and bibliographic edits, but the section sequence and Appendices A–E retain their structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds the method schematic in Figure 2 and ablation Tables 4–5. Existing figures are renumbered and repositioned, with caption styling and spacing adjustments. The retained plots and table structures are substantially preserved.

improvement.justification: The new ablations provide empirical support for previously untested representation choices, and Figure 2 plus the attention-processing qualification improve clarity. The main findings remain unchanged. Some default scores in Tables 4–5 differ from Table 3's averages without explaining the aggregation or run differences, limiting the reporting improvement.
